lots.what_it_is: Singer Featherweight 222K free-arm portable electric sewing machine (made at Kilbowie, Scotland, about 1953 to 1964) in its black carry case, with foot controller, presser feet and attachments, embroidery hoop, a red tray of notions and a replaced black power lead. Catalogued only as 'portable Singer cased electric sewing machine, going order', so the scarcer 222K model is not named.
lots.score_reason: A genuine 222K, the scarcer free-arm Featherweight. Australian auction results in the last 24 months are A$300 to A$1,250 hammer (median about A$440), so a real value of roughly A$300 to A$600 at a local auction. Not scored higher because two comparable under-described lots made only A$300 and the replaced lead and running condition are unchecked.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 2: oval gold Singer medallion with a clearly legible 222K cartouche beneath it; SINGER decal on the arm; a small gold stamp left of the badge ending 'BRITAIN' (Made in Great Britain, partly legible); the base is in two parts with a seam under the bed, which is the 222K free-arm bed extension. Serial number not visible. Photo 1: tall black case with the foot controller clipped in the lid, a tan box (looks empty), a box of presser feet and attachments, a white box holding two metal embroidery hoop rings, and a red tray. Photo 3: modern black flex with a moulded Australian 3-pin plug (not original), red tray of thread and notions, and a folded or rolled paper item at the side (possibly the instruction booklet, not legible).
lots.condition: Machine glossy with decals largely intact and light wear to the bed and base; case scuffed with a worn lining; power lead replaced with a modern one, so an electrical safety check is advisable; Armitage says going order but I could not see it run; serial, bobbin case and bed extension latch unchecked.

lots.what_it_is: Pictorial painted bark cloth (tapa, called siapo or ngatu) from Wallis (Uvea), Wallis and Futuna, about 53 x 200 cm, in two scenes: a village scene (house, seated women with shell necklaces, a standing woman, pineapple, palms, flowers) and a sea scene (outrigger sailing canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail, lobster, crab, octopus, fish, ray), with wavy red-brown and black and white geometric borders and black cloth hanging sleeves at both ends. Mua is a district of Wallis, so the title's 'by Mua Wallis' misreads a place name as a maker.
lots.score_reason: Credible identification as a rare pictorial Wallis type (Te Papa holds a near twin attributed to the 1960s), but the realistic Australian auction value is modest: generic tapa made A$10 to A$320 in the last 24 months, an early pictorial Tongan cloth passed at A$500, and a near-identical Wallis land-sea runner passed at EUR 80 in 2010. The upside is in a specialist Pacific sale (Webb's sold a smaller pictorial Uvea piece for NZD 950 in 2023). Scored for roughly A$150 to A$400, discounted for unverified age and the optimistic dealer ask.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 3 reads 'Mua Wallis' on the canoe sail (a place inscription, not a signature). The composition matches Te Papa FE012568 (record opened, https://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/object/1086286: Wallis and Futuna, attributed to the 1960s, 762 x 1985 mm, 'a rare example of tapa decorated with pictorial references', the same canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail and a village scene, bought from a French brocante in 2010, no price) and the 1stdibs dealer piece (same two-scene layout, island name on the canoe). It also resembles a narrow 'terre-mer' Wallis runner (43 x 165 cm) that passed at EUR 80 in Marseille in 2010, which suggests a repeated decorative or trade type rather than a one-off. Black sleeves are stitched to both ends for hanging; the dark red-brown pigment is glossy (a traditional glossy dye or a later coating, not determinable from the photos).
lots.condition: Looks intact in the photos, with no holes or tears visible; creases, folds and wavy uneven edges; glossy finish on the dark pigment; hanging sleeves stitched on. The back is not shown, so staining, insect damage, brittleness or repairs cannot be judged. Age unverified.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: long teak top with lipped edges, narrowing slightly towards the ends, tapered round legs and a five-slat lower shelf. Enlarged crops of the underside (photo 2) show a pale veneered underside, legs fixed at the corners and the slatted shelf on rails; no maker's label, stamp, paper tag or 'Made in Denmark' mark is visible. Small auction labels on the top.
lots.condition: Good in the photos: top clean and even in colour with no obvious rings, burns or deep scratches; joints look tight; legs and slats intact. Needs a close look for veneer lifting at the edges, sun-fading and wobble.

lots.guide_summary: Range A$90 to A$490 across 12 same-type entries: 11 SOLD (Gowans, Hobart, A$100 to A$490 hammer, with the closest surfboard and slatted-shelf forms at A$280 to A$440 in 2026; Leonard Joel, Melbourne, A$90 to A$340) and 1 UNSOLD (low estimate A$200, then sold at A$90). No same-type ASKING survives: two overseas Chairish asks (A$447 and A$645) are category guides only. Plain or smaller tables sold A$50 to A$260. All AUD apart from the asks (1 USD = A$1.437, 2026-10-16). Gowans prices are hammer with 19.8% premium extra.
lots.working: keep_max_hammer: the closest same-form SOLD results in similar condition within 24 months are A$280 (Gowans lot 619, 2026-09-25), A$280 (Leonard Joel lot 1227, 2025-07-31), A$380 (Gowans lot 705) and A$440 (Gowans lot 782); lowest A$280. 280 / 1.22 = 229.5, rounded down to $225 (all-in $274.50). The A$160 Melbourne table of the same length was excluded for its worn top. flip_max_hammer: likely resale = median of those four (280, 280, 380, 440) = A$330 hammer; less 15% seller commission ($49.50) and $0 outbound postage (resell through a local room, buyer collects) = $280.50; 280.50 / 2.44 = 115.0, rounded down to $110 (all-in $134.20). If it had to be carted to Gowans in Hobart, allow about $80 transport, which cuts the flip max to about $80. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). Armitage's own past results were not checked because WebSearch was capped for this run.

lots.question_for_armitage: Could you please check lot 80: (1) any maker's stamp, label or 'Made in Denmark' mark under the top or on the shelf rails; (2) the veneer edges and lipping for lifting or chips, and the top for water rings or sun-fading under the lights; (3) whether the legs are tight and the table sits level without wobble.
